newsitem.title: INDIA: India's CRISIL chief expects rise in debt issues.
newsitem.headline: India's CRISIL chief expects rise in debt issues.

text.p: Indian bond issues, becoming popular against depressed equity markets, are seen gaining ground as more and more investors switch to debt, India's premier credit rating agency chief said on Tuesday.
"We strongly believe that the debt market will happen and in a big way," R. Ravimohan, managing director of Credit Rating Information Services of India Ltd (CRISIL) told an investment conference.
CRISIL is India's largest credit rating agency.
In the past few months, new bond floats have mopped up 55 billion rupees.
Ravimohan said the Indian debt market had seen a resurgence in debt issues over the past two years indicating investor disappointment over the performance of the country's stock markets.

Concerns over political stability -- with the advent of a new government last June --, a liquidity crunch and a diasappointing 1996/97 budget have dragged down equities in the last couple of months, analysts said.
"Portfolio allocation between equity and debt has most certainly become a recent phenomenon for retail investors," Ravimohan said.
